trigger: sanitize_url_userinfo's scheme-boundary detection (url.find("://")) finds the FIRST '://' anywhere in the string, including one embedded inside a later query-string value
summary: Adversarial input (compiled, standalone-reproduced by security-guardian): 'myuser:mypassword@10.0.0.5:9000/db?ssl_ca=https://ca.corp.example/root.pem' -- a schemeless credential form whose query string carries a TLS CA-bundle URL as a value. The nested 'https://' inside that query value is found by url.find("://") BEFORE the real credential is ever considered, pushing authority_start past the real '@' and past end of any plausible userinfo region; the at_pos >= authority_start guard then suppresses the strip entirely and the credential is returned in full, unsanitized. NOT FIXED in this session -- this is the SECOND round-2 defect found by Gate 8b for this same function (session hit the 2-fix-round cap per standing coordinator authority: 'if a fix round doesn't resolve after a reasonable attempt or two, stop iterating and flag it'). security-guardian reports a verified fix shape exists (restrict scheme detection to a bounded prefix scan rather than find() over the whole string) but it was not applied or re-verified this session. FLAGGED FOR HUMAN REVIEW: a proper fix likely needs the scheme search bounded to characters before the first '/', ':', or '@' from position 0, not a global find() -- but given this function's history (3 distinct defects across 2 fix-round redesigns, each independently found by a different combination of reviewers), a full RFC 3986-aware parse (or a well-tested existing URL library) may be the more defensible fix than a 4th hand-rolled patch. Round 2 (this commit) is still shipped as a net improvement over round 1 -- it closes 9fb955c39's 3 defects and 2 further round-1 regressions -- but the sanitizer is NOT fully closed.

trigger: sanitize_url_userinfo strips '@' first, then searches the RESULT (already-mutated string) for '?'/'#' -- breaks when the query string itself contains a later '@'
summary: Adversarial input (hand-traced against all 10 existing tests by cpp-expert): 'clickhouse://host:9000/yuzu?user=admin@corp.com&password=s3cr3t' -> current code returns 'clickhouse://corp.com&password=s3cr3t' (password leaks in plaintext). Root cause: at_pos is computed on raw url and finds the '@' inside 'admin@corp.com' (the LAST '@' in the string); everything up to and including it -- including the real '?' query delimiter -- is discarded before the query-strip step ever runs, so the query-strip finds no '?' and the trailing 'password=s3cr3t' survives verbatim. NOT FIXED in this session (2-fix-round cap reached; this is the second distinct new bypass Gate 8b found in round 2, alongside g8b-sanitizer-scheme-boundary). cpp-expert supplied a verified candidate fix (compute at_pos and qf both against the ORIGINAL url, union the two removal ranges instead of applying them sequentially) hand-checked against all 10 existing cases + this new one, but it was NOT applied or independently re-verified this session -- applying it now would be an unreviewed 3rd redesign attempt, exactly the pattern this cap exists to stop. FLAGGED FOR HUMAN REVIEW alongside g8b-sanitizer-scheme-boundary; both likely need the SAME fix shape (compute-both-cuts-on-the-original-string-then-union) since both stem from the identical composability defect: sequential string mutation across two independent search-and-strip passes.

Closed by commit fd8ea8538: scheme detection bounded to a plain RFC-3986-shaped prefix scan from position 0 (ALPHA *(ALPHA/DIGIT/"+"/"-"/".") immediately followed by "://"), so a "://" embedded in a later query value can no longer be mistaken for the real scheme delimiter. Independently reproduced as still-open against the pre-fix compiled object by two external adversarial reviewers (Kimi, Codex, /home/dgr/advrev-4028) before the fix landed, and re-verified leak-free against the post-fix compiled object after (standalone probe linked against src_settings_model.cpp.o, plus new test_settings_model.cpp regression coverage: 'does not leak userinfo when a later query value embeds its own "://"').

Closed by commit fd8ea8538: both the userinfo-'@' cut point and the query/fragment-start cut point are now computed against the ORIGINAL url and unioned, never sequentially against a once-mutated result. When the two ranges overlap (query/fragment start at or before the apparent userinfo-ending '@' -- the exact ambiguous shape this finding exploited), everything from the authority boundary onward is dropped rather than guessed. Independently reproduced as still-open against the pre-fix compiled object by two external adversarial reviewers (Kimi, Codex, /home/dgr/advrev-4028) before the fix landed, and re-verified leak-free against the post-fix compiled object after (standalone probe linked against src_settings_model.cpp.o, plus two new test_settings_model.cpp regression cases covering this shape and the analogous unescaped-'?' shape).
